data.title: Gold, Silver Futures Post Weekly Losses — Market Talk
data.description: Gold futures hold their ground in choppy trading as a below-estimate U.S. producer price reading and steadying oil prices ease inflation concerns that sank the metals the previous session. Silver falls to a new 52-week low. "Gold is trying to get back on its feet after getting shot up yesterday," Phil Flynn of the Price Futures Group says in a note. The market is reading the Middle East conflict through the price of oil, he says. "Higher crude means higher inflation, which means a tougher Fed, which hurts a metal that pays no interest." Front month gold settles up $1.30 in New York at $3,879.70 a troy ounce for a 4.5% weekly loss. Silver falls 1.9% to $49.031 a troy ounce, its lowest close in a year and down 5.4% on the week. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: House Oversight Chair calls for possible ban on government officials’ prediction market bets over insider trading concerns
data.description:
The Republican chair of the House Oversight Committee is calling for new limits on government officials' use of prediction markets, including the possibility of an outright ban, amid growing concerns that public officials could use insider information to profit from bets on the platforms.

On Friday, the committee released findings from an investigation it launched in May into insider trading risks in prediction markets among government officials, military personnel, and those with security clearances. The committee sifted through 1,700 pages of documents and also received five bipartisan staff briefings from prediction market companies, said Chair James Comer, R-Ky.

Concerns in Washington have intensified over the past year, particularly after an active-duty U.S. Army soldier who used confidential information to place bets on Polymarket ahead of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro's capture. Thereafter, others in government have also been found using inside information to make money on bets on prediction markets, including the White House's former teleprompter operator. Political candidates have also faced allegations of insider trading on the platforms.

"Congress must consider additional reforms to prevent public corruption and restore the American people's trust in government," Comer said on Friday.

Those reforms should be legislation that restricts which bets federal employees, lawmakers and congressional staff can place on prediction markets — or an outright ban, the committee said.

"Whether it's an outright prohibition on trading on prediction markets or restrictions on some subset of contracts like government-related contracts, applying these restrictions to officials in all branches of government would strengthen ethical expectations that government personnel should not personally and financially benefit from access to non-public information associated with their work as government servants…" according to the memo.

Congress should also have a role in encouraging prediction market companies and federal agencies to share necessary information to enforce restrictions, the committee said.

Both major prediction market companies — Kalshi and Polymarket — have said they have taken steps to tighten controls to prevent government officials from using inside information. Lawmakers have also begun addressing the issue themselves. In April, the Senate voted to pass a resolution to ban members from trading on prediction markets.

data.title: Matt Hagan Is One Race Away from NHRA History on FOX Sports' FS1 as American Rebel Light Beer Rallies Fans Behind Tony Stewart Racing - Win Hagan Win!
data.description:
With one event remaining, the 2026 regular-season champion enters Pomona with a 39-point lead and a shot at his fifth Funny Car world title; American Rebel's TSR partnership began during his 2023 championship season.

American Rebel Light Beer Is Ready to Celebrate as Top Fuel Standout and True American Rebel Leah Pruett Aims to "Finish the Job" at Pomona - Finish Leah Finish!

POMONA, CA, PROVO, UT, AND NASHVLLE, TN / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / American Rebel Holdings, Inc. , through American Rebel Light Beer - America's Patriotic Beer - is taking its "Win Hagan Win!" rally to the season finale as Matt Hagan pursues a historic fifth NHRA Funny Car world championship. With one event remaining, the four-time world champion and 2026 regular-season champion enters this weekend's In-N-Out Burger NHRA Finals at In-N-Out Burger Pomona Dragstrip with a 39-point lead over Jordan Vandergriff.

American Rebel first partnered with Hagan and Tony Stewart Racing (TSR) in August 2023, announcing a multiyear agreement that included selected primary sponsorships and associate support. That November, Hagan captured his fourth Funny Car world championship at Pomona. Now, that continuing relationship connects American Rebel Light Beer with his pursuit of number five.

"American Rebel joined the TSR family in 2023, the year Matt won his fourth world championship. Now we're behind him as he goes after number five," said Andy Ross, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Rebel Holdings, Inc. "Matt is a true American Rebel. He has earned this opportunity, and we're ready to cheer him on and raise a cold American Rebel Light Beer with fans who love racing and love the USA. Win Hagan Win! Win Rebel Win!"

Matt Hagan - Four World Titles. One Race Remaining. The Chase for Five.

A fifth world title would move Hagan ahead of Kenny Bernstein and Don Prudhomme into sole possession of second place on the all-time Funny Car championship list, behind only John Force.

Hagan's 2026 campaign includes four event victories and seven final-round appearances, highlighted by his 59th career Funny Car victory at Rockingham and a runner-up finish in Dallas. He returns to Pomona with eight event wins at the track, including three NHRA Finals victories and five Winternationals titles. In April, he defeated Ron Capps there to win NHRA's 1,000th Funny Car event.

"We're here, we're racing, and we've got a shot," Hagan said. "I think that's all you can really hope for: to just have a real shot at this championship."

A Season of Racing and National Brand Exposure for American Rebel

American Rebel's 2026 program combines selected primary sponsorships, associate branding, national television coverage, digital content and trackside fan engagement. The November 12-15 finale also brings a chance to cheer for Top Fuel standout Leah Pruett and toast TSR owner Tony Stewart's Robert E. Petersen Lifetime Achievement Award.

At Brainerd on August 23, Hagan drove the American Rebel Light Beer Dodge//SRT Hellcat Funny Car to victory and moved into the points lead. At Seattle on July 26, Pruett took the American Rebel Light Beer Top Fuel dragster to the final round, bringing the branded car into the closing showdown of a nationally televised event.

The scale of the opportunity was especially clear at October's Midwest Nationals, where Hagan reached the semifinals in the American Rebel Light Beer Funny Car. According to World Wide Technology Raceway, FOX's Sunday race telecast averaged 1.896 million viewers and peaked at 3.247 million, following a sold-out Saturday at the track. That weekend put American Rebel's primary-branded Funny Car into a major NHRA broadcast event with a national audience reaching into the millions.

Those moments give the Company a continuing story to share with adult consumers, distributors, retailers and hospitality accounts. American Rebel's objective is to turn recognition of its race-car branding into recognition of the beer itself - and give fans a reason to ask for American Rebel Light Beer wherever they gather to watch and celebrate.

"When Matt wins with American Rebel Light Beer on the car, or Leah takes our branded dragster to the final round, our beer becomes part of a moment fans remember," Ross added. "We have built this relationship over multiple seasons because the fit is real. Matt and Leah compete with conviction and live life on their own terms. That is the American Rebel attitude, and it belongs on our cans and in our brand."

Leah Pruett Is Ready to Finish the Job - Finish Leah Finish!

Pruett arrives at her home track following a runner-up finish in Las Vegas and a comeback season that included her 13th career Top Fuel victory at the New England Nationals - her first win since becoming a mother. She returned to full-time competition in 2026 after two seasons away and has announced plans to step back from full-time driving in 2027 to focus on her family.

Her focus for Pomona is clear: "finish the job." In pre-race comments published by Dragzine, Pruett explained that she wants to win the World Finals after finishing runner-up in her previous appearance at the event. American Rebel is cheering for a winning finish to a season that has shown her competitive drive and commitment to family.

"A Top Fuel driver and a mom - how much more American Rebel can you get?" Ross said. "Leah has the courage to chase a win at more than 300 miles an hour and the strength to make her own decisions about racing and family. We respect that, we celebrate that, and we want to see her finish this season in the winner's circle."

Cheers to TSR Team Owner Tony Stewart

American Rebel also raises a cold American Rebel Light Beer to TSR team owner Tony Stewart, who recently received the Robert E. Petersen Lifetime Achievement Award from the Petersen Automotive Museum during the 2026 SEMA Industry Honors at the BleauLive Theater inside Fontainebleau Las Vegas. The award recognizes lasting contributions to the automotive industry and motorsports and places Stewart among past honorees including Wally Parks, Carroll Shelby and Richard Petty.

With three NASCAR Cup championships, an IndyCar title, USAC championships and victories in NHRA Top Fuel, Stewart has built a racing legacy across disciplines. Through his race teams and his ownership of Eldora Speedway, he has also helped create opportunities for drivers, crews and fans.

"Tony Stewart has always embodied the American Rebel spirit. He has made his own way through this sport, won at the highest levels and kept taking on the next challenge," Ross said. "This is a well-deserved honor for a man who has given so much to racing. We're proud to be part of the TSR family, and we're raising a cold American Rebel Light Beer to him. Cheers to Tony Stewart!"

Stewart's recognition adds another reason to celebrate ahead of Pomona. Hagan delivered TSR's first NHRA world championship in 2023; a fifth world title for Hagan this weekend would also give TSR its second.

Tune In to the NHRA Finals and Raise an American Rebel Light Beer for Matt and Leah

American Rebel invites fans 21 and older to stock the cooler, gather with fellow racing fans and cheer for Hagan, Pruett and TSR as NHRA's 75th anniversary season reaches its finale. From the grandstands to watch parties across the country, America's Patriotic Beer is ready to toast the racers, the fans and the American Rebel spirit. Cheers to Tony Stewart.

FS1 is scheduled to carry qualifying coverage Sunday, November 15, from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Eastern, followed by finals coverage from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern. Additional FS1 and FS2 replays extend the opportunity to follow the action. Visit NHRA's television schedule for current listings; broadcast times are subject to change.

Find product information and the beer locator at AmericanRebelBeer.com, and ask your local retailer or favorite bar for American Rebel Light Beer.

data.title: PermRock Royalty Trust 3Q 2026 — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
PermRock Royalty Trust’s net profits income received fell year over year as $435,000 in capital reserves was withheld, compared with a $93,242 release a year earlier; before capital reserve activity, net profits income increased as higher realized oil prices more than offset lower oil and gas volumes, lower gas prices and higher costs.

Business Highlights

  • Production: Oil sales volumes decreased 20.9% and natural gas sales volumes fell 33.9%, primarily due to natural decline; oil volumes also reflected shut-in wells during regulatory workovers.
  • Prices: Average realized oil price rose to $90.75 per barrel from $63.58; natural gas price declined to $0.84 per Mcf from $1.88.
  • Workovers: T2S completed workovers on 22 shut-in wells and one plugging and abandonment operation; its approximately $0.7 million 2026 budget was spent by September 30.
  • Outlook: T2S expects production increases from workovers to be realized during the fourth quarter of 2026.

data.title: Pennsylvania reports seventh measles-linked death as cases rise
data.description:
Pennsylvania health officials on Friday reported the state's seventh measles-associated death this year as the outbreak continued to spread.

The state has recorded 1,542 confirmed measles cases as of November 13, including 305 hospitalizations, the Pennsylvania Department of Health said.

Pennsylvania has been the epicenter of the US measles outbreak in 2026, accounting for a substantial share of infections reported nationwide.

Measles is a highly contagious viral infection that causes symptoms such as fever, cough and a characteristic rash, and can lead to severe complications like pneumonia and encephalitis.

It can be prevented through the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, which is about 97% effective after two doses.

data.title: Uber Says Personal Data Was Exposed in Third-Party Data Breach
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Uber Technologies is notifying users that their personal information was exposed in a breach involving one of the company's service providers.

The transportation company said an unauthorized third party had compromised a service provider's internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account, according to a notice on the California attorney general's website dated Tuesday.

Uber immediately severed data connections with the service provider and launched an investigation after being notified about the breach Oct. 9.

Four days later, the investigation determined the unauthorized party had used the compromised credentials to access Uber data connected to the service provider.

Uber is providing affected individuals with access to credit monitoring and fraud assistance at no charge, according to the notice.

Uber didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

STOCKTON, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Health Net, one of California's most experienced Medi-Cal managed care health plans and company of Centene Corporation (), today announced a $3 million investment in the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund. The funding will provide grants and low-interest loans to accelerate affordable housing developments and support the creation of at least 75 affordable homes for Stockton families facing some of the region's most significant housing challenges.

"A home is so much more than a roof overhead. It's the place where families feel safe, children can grow and learn, and people can focus on their health and well-being," said Dorothy M. Seleski, Medi-Cal Plan President at Health Net. "Too many families in our communities are struggling to find housing they can afford. By partnering with the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund, we're helping create more opportunities for families to put down roots, build stability and look toward the future with greater confidence. Together, we're investing in healthier communities by helping more people find a place to call home."

The investment will support community-driven housing developments, with a focus on serving families facing the greatest barriers to affordable housing, including households earning between 30% and 50% of the area median income.

"When local organizations unite around a shared goal, communities move forward," said San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund Board Chair Gary Singh. "Health Net's investment will help transform plans into homes for local families while encouraging broader community participation in addressing the region's housing needs."

The investment will support eligible projects through January 2029, from planning through construction.

"Investments in affordable housing are investments in the health, strength and future of our communities," said San Joaquin County Supervisor Robert Rickman. "By bringing public, private and community partners together, we can help more San Joaquin County families find stable housing and create lasting opportunity across the region."

In Sacramento and San Joaquin counties, Health Net has invested a combined $11 million in affordable housing and related initiatives, including $2 million to Stanislaus Equity Partners, Inc. (STEP) and $3 million to Fairview Terrace. By supporting developments at every stage, from planning and financing to construction and occupancy, Health Net is helping expand access to affordable housing, strengthen local communities and create the conditions for better health across the region.

About Health Net

Founded in California more than 45 years ago, Health Net, LLC ("Health Net"), a company of Centene Corporation, believes that every person deserves a safety net for their health, regardless of age, income, employment status or current state of health. Today, we provide health plans for individuals, families, businesses of every size and people who qualify for Medi-Cal or Medicare. With more than 117,000 of our network providers, Health Net serves more than three million members across the state. We also offer access to substance abuse programs, behavioral health services and managed healthcare products related to prescription drugs. We make these health plans and services available through Health Net and its subsidiaries: Health Net of California, Inc., Health Net Life Insurance Company and Health Net Community Solutions, Inc. These entities are wholly owned subsidiaries of Centene Corporation (), a leading healthcare enterprise committed to transforming the health of the communities we serve, one person at a time. Health Net and Centene Corporation employ more than 5,700 people in California who work at one of five regional Talent Hub offices. For more information, visit www.HealthNet.com.

data.title: US extends shipping law waiver 90 days, to allow freer movement of oil, commodities
data.description:
President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Reuters reported on Thursday that industry sources said the administration would extend the waiver on the more than 100-year-old Jones Act.

It has been the longest waiver in the history of the shipping law.

The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched the war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. In August, it extended the waiver but mandated that decisions would be made on a case-by-case basis, a stipulation continued through the latest waiver.

The ⁠Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies and crewed by American workers. Allowing the waiver aims to lower gas, diesel and fertilizer prices driven up by the war on Iran by increasing shipping flexibility and reducing transport bottlenecks.

The length of waivers has been limited in the past as the Jones Act is supported by the domestic shipbuilding business, a powerful lobby across the country.

data.title: Virgin Galactic Touches 52-Week Low After Update on Financing, Commercial Operations
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Shares of Virgin Galactic hit a 52-week low after the company discussed plans for its financing and commercial operations and reported quarterly results.

The stock down 27%, to $1.96, midday Friday after touching an intraday low of $1.95. It has fallen about 39% this year.

Virgin Galactic said it expects to increase capacity to 150 spaceflights a year by the end of 2028. The company began booking a limited tranche of Spaceflight Expeditions at $850,000 a seat.

In October, the company said it expected commercial spaceflights to start in the second quarter of 2027. It previously delayed the target to February 2027 from the fourth quarter of 2026.

In a securities filing Thursday, Virgin Galactic said it intended to exchange stock for 2.5% convertible senior notes due 2027 and that it entered an open market sale agreement for the potential sale of up to $250 million of stock "as part of a comprehensive plan to support its operations and growth initiatives."

On Friday, the company said in a filing it entered an agreement with a noteholder for a $12.5 million exchange.

Third-quarter revenue was $427,000, up from $365,000 a year earlier, the company reported Thursday afternoon. Loss was 39 cents a share, compared with a loss of $1.09 a share a year earlier.

Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com
